statistic.name: other
statistic.notes: Rasch-Welch t-test DIF contrasts by gender (male vs. female) and ethnicity (Caucasian vs. non-Caucasian); contrasts >.64 and statistically significant counted as substantial. Of 22 items, 21 showed negligible DIF; one item with substantial DIF on both (and poor OUTFIT) was removed, giving the 21-item scale.

sample.description: General public sample from the development study; 58 persons with extreme INFIT/OUTFIT were excluded before item analysis.

source.citation: Libarkin, J. C., Gold, A. U., Harris, S. E., McNeal, K. S., & Bowles, R. P. (2018). A new, valid measure of climate change understanding: Associations with risk perception. Climatic Change, 150(3-4), 403-416. Online supplement.

needs_check: Confirm whether n = 1111 counts respondents before or after the 58 exclusions.
